agent.name: Emerging Technology Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Technology intelligence and contextual landscape monitoring

analytical_question: Where does grounded AI assistance sit in the landscape for human-reviewed retail returns answers, and what should the retailer monitor?
general_et_finding: As of 2026-11-15, generative AI assistance is available through established office ecosystems (S1/S2), but product availability is not evidence of reliable performance in a specific task. S3 supports the possibility of benefits with heterogeneous outcomes in customer support. Inference: evaluate application-specific evidence rather than assign a universal maturity score. Current industry adoption rates, investment trends and comparative prices are unknown in this packet.
application_finding: Assess. The strongest conventional competitor is approved FAQ/macros with policy retrieval. Grounded AI can draft more variable answers, while the conventional baseline may be simpler for routine questions (inference). Microsoft Copilot (S1) and Gemini in qualifying Workspace services (S2) are ecosystem candidates only if they fit the actual support workspace; neither source establishes CRM suitability. A retrieval-plus-LLM workflow is another architectural option. Complements are a versioned returns knowledge base, access controls, escalation rules and human approval. S3 is closer in task domain than for syllabus checking, but is not a local returns-policy benchmark.
organization_specific_finding: Hypothetical online retailer: remain at Assess for the next 90 days. The decisive signal is reliable retrieval of the currently applicable returns policy with fewer total handling minutes and no incorrect refund promises in a pre-specified local test. CRM permissions, integration, costs and policy ownership are unknown. Customer-facing policy commitments make freshness and escalation more consequential than syllabus omission coverage. Industry adoption, investment and jurisdiction-specific legal obligations remain unverified.

evidence.claim: Grounding, integration and licensing differ across Copilot experiences; access is scoped by permissions.
evidence.notes: Vendor capability documentation, not independent accuracy or ROI evidence. No tenant entitlement or price verified.

evidence.claim: For covered qualifying Workspace services, content access follows permissions and customer data is not used for model training without prior permission or instruction.
evidence.notes: Applies to specified covered services and editions, not all consumer or third-party tools. No comparative accuracy evidence.

evidence.claim: Study of 5,172 customer-support agents reports a 15% mean improvement in issues resolved per hour, with heterogeneous effects.
evidence.notes: Historical single-company deployment; not a 2026 market adoption measure, syllabus accuracy result, or cost-saving guarantee. Do not mix earlier working-paper estimates with final article.

evidence.claim: Cross-sectoral companion to the voluntary AI Risk Management Framework for generative AI.
evidence.notes: Guidance, not a binding law, product certification or proof of local compliance.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: S3 is relevant customer-support evidence but comes from a different historical deployment; heterogeneous effects and task differences prevent transfer of its mean gain to this retailer.
S1 and S2 are vendor claims about their own systems, not a head-to-head benchmark; no industry/consulting dataset or independent current market adoption estimate was verified.
Stale/hype-sensitive claim: existing enterprise subscription makes a grounded workflow free. Product, edition, connector and usage terms must be checked; total cost remains unknown.
All organizational profiles and decision gates are proposed scenarios, not field observations.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the source types and their limited scope; moderate confidence that a baseline comparison is appropriate; low confidence in local cost, accuracy, performance trends or a vendor ranking. S1/S2 describe current documentation checked 2026-11-15; S3 is historical deployment evidence published 2025-02-04; S4 is guidance published 2024-07-26. Retrieval does not refresh the age of the underlying evidence.
value_opportunity_implication: Potential to reduce answer drafting and correction time. Compare against approved macros on matched policy questions, including exceptions and stale-policy traps. Measure total handling time and incorrect promises; no measured local savings are available.
risk_governance_implication: Incorrect refund promises and stale policy retrieval are priority risks. The policy owner must govern versions; human reviewers retain approval and autonomous refunds remain out of scope. S4 is guidance, not legal approval.
recommendation_management_implication: Position: Assess. Keep approved FAQ/macros as the baseline. Request versioned returns policies, a labeled question set and CRM/tenant controls. A verified policy refresh process plus matched local evidence could justify a Trial candidate handoff to Adoption and Implementing specialists. Do not authorize automatic customer replies or refunds.
change_monitoring_triggers: Owner: IT/procurement lead (proposed). Cadence: before evaluation and monthly. Signal: a change in applicable licensing, connector access, permission scope or usage charges, or a vendor source unrefreshed for more than 30 days. Action: recheck S1/S2 and the actual tenant; suspend any free-cost assumption and revise the shortlist.

Owner: returns policy owner (proposed). Cadence: every policy revision and daily during evaluation. Signal: stale policy citation or any incorrect refund promise. Action: pause affected evaluation outputs, update retrieval sources and rerun exception cases; retain Assess.

Owner: customer-support quality lead (proposed). Cadence: weekly during a controlled evaluation. Signal: zero incorrect promises in the agreed evaluation set, lower total handling-plus-correction time than approved macros, and verified CRM/access terms. Action: propose Trial candidate handoff; also investigate any complaint increase before expanding. These are unvalidated proposed gates.

Owner: landscape analyst (proposed). Cadence: quarterly and on material publication or policy notices. Signal: directly comparable independent evidence, new competing workflow, or revised guidance. Action: update S3/S4, contrary evidence and relative alternatives; legal questions go to qualified review.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request returns-policy versions, exceptions, labeled support cases, current macro baseline, CRM permissions, budget and jurisdiction.
Abstain from local ROI, product ranking, legal assurance or autonomous refund approval. No real support workflow was tested.
